procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism before applying for a certificate. Registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added; it takes about 3 working days. Traders can apply only for goods bought from a registered factory.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Apply for the preferential Certificate of Origin for India through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service on the Ministry of Foreign Trade portal (moet.gov.ae or eservices.moec.gov.ae). The service runs 24/7 and processing takes about one working day.

Complete the application form with the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product. Each item must qualify separately. The issuing authority may ask for detailed cost sheets and conduct a factory visit.
Upload the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee. The fee for the Certificate of Origin for India ranges from AED 10 to AED 200 depending on the invoice value.
Submit the application and await approval. If the application is returned with comments, correct and resubmit. Once approved, print the certificate.

The certificate of origin is valid for 12 months from the date of issue and covers one import. It should be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export. A certificate can be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.

Ensure the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed. The importer keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing and must answer a customs request within 10 working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Mansha interprets '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+'.
The value addition threshold is 5 percentage points lower when the Ex-Works price is used as the basis.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

Factory registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone; a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible. This is an interpretation and should be confirmed with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
